Figure 2:Kling-MLLM architecture. Multimodal inputs are encoded by visual and
audio paths into aligned continuous tokens, delimited by modality boundary
markers, anchored with physical timestamps, and interleaved with text before
entering the LLM backbone. The audio path illustrates the dual-branch
Mel–VAE tower used in larger variants. ‘Sync A-V’ denotes synchronized audio–video input.

Figure 3:Two captions of a 17.7 s clip fromMeridian. Circled numbers link seven facts across the frames, timeline, and captions. The fluent caption reads well but omits or misrepresents key details. The generation-oriented caption preserves shot timing, audiovisual alignment, and visible text, including mirror-reversed lettering.

Figure 4:Reference-grounded captioning on a 22.5 s clip fromMeridian, given two portraits (IMG_1, IMG_2) and a voice track (AUD_1). The caption states each binding with its scope and writes out everything the references cannot supply. The timeline shows who is on screen and when PERSON_1 speaks. Circled numbers mark where each property of the semantic contract applies, contrasting typical shortcuts with correct formulations.

images.caption: Figure 7:Three-stage training pipeline for our RMs, starting from Kling-MLLM-27B.Stage 1adapts the vision encoder and aligner with the LLM frozen for low-level artifact perception;Stage 2trains the General Reward Model (GRM) with cold-start SFT and RL with verifiable rewards for explainable evaluation;Stage 3initializes the Decision Reward Model (DRM) from the GRM and performs decision-head warm-up, unified pointwise–pairwise SFT with TA grounding, and symmetry calibration with gated inference for fast multi-dimensional scoring.
